sections.heading: Govinda Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 17 February, 2023
content: 1. Heard Sri A.K. Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri O.P. Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. The instant anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with a prayer to release him on anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 0372 of 2022, under Sections 379 , 411 , 419 , 420 , 467 , 468 , 471 IPC, Sections 3 / 57 / 70 of U.P. Sub Mineral (Concession) Manual, Sections 4 / 21 of Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, Sections 3 / 4 of Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act, Sections 66C , 66D of Information Technology Act, Police Station Robertsganj, District Sonbhadra.

3. As per prosecution case, a mobile team of Mineral Department was checking the vehicle carrying the gitti; they checked certain vehicles and verified the papers given by its driver, from the departmental m-check app; it was found that no MM11 for carrying minerals through vehicle no. UP 64 AT 6234 was ever issued; the driver on the spot revealed that on the instructions of the truck owner-Sufiyan Ahmad, it was being carried with a permit MM11; as papers were found false and fabricated, therefore, the truck was seized and FIR was lodged.

4. It is contended on behalf of the applicant that though his name appears in the body of the FIR, however, there is no allegation of any kind against him and therefore, the FIR has not been registered against him; it is also contended that the applicant though is not named as an accused, is being harassed by the police on different pretext and that he apprehends his arrest; he merely worked at the crusher as a clerk and he had no role to play in this episode of carrying grit (gitti) without permit on the basis of forged papers.
5. The application for anticipatory bail is opposed by learned AGA for the State, however, factual matrix of the matter could not be refuted.

6. In case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra , (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by the Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.

7. In the instant case, I considered submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case. In my view, a case for anticipatory bail is made out.

8. Let the applicant, Govinda Kumar involved in the aforesaid case crime number be released on anticipatory bail till submission of police report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties each of the same amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned, subject to the conditions as below:-
9. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.
10. It is made clear that observations made herein shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion at any stage of the case based on material before him.
Order Date :- 17.2.2023 #Vikram/-
